stage.a: MVP — first release meeting rolling-wave §4's independent-use bar (cold start from a published artifact, real ingest/query lifecycle, solo-scale `pulsedb repair`), v2 bar unmet, "third release" not a criterion, and the missing date correct per §5.
stage.b: mvp — same three-part §4 bar met for the first time, v2 bar unmet (promise unchanged, journey now fully real, no contract break), "not counted", and the absent date/label correct.

increment_type.a: Rung 1 journey gate passes — not an `internal-enabler`; the `user:` line is an actor reaching an observable outcome, near-verbatim the ACCEPT row in demo-authoring §3.4, and rejecting it would be §3.3's false-reject.
increment_type.b: Rung 1 journey gate passes — not an `internal-enabler`; the `user:` line is "the accept side of demo-authoring §3.4's own worked pair".

d_class.a: `bone`, overruling the declared `flesh`, on rung 2 bone-touch — `src/storage/segment.rs` is inside the on-disk-segment-format bone's registered surface ("the declared class is a claim; the touch surface is a fact"); A then states rungs 3 and 4 are not reached.
d_class.b: `bone`, overruling the declared `flesh`, on rung 2 bone-touch for the identical reason; B additionally runs rung 3 and finds an independent bone-by-creation (bones category 5, trust boundaries & destructive operations) in the unregistered new file `src/retention/policy.rs`.

risk_tier.a: Gate warranted, family `destructive` (permanent segment removal a test failure cannot undo, not bounded-and-locally-reversible), touch surface `src/retention/**,src/storage/segment.rs` with `src/cli/commands.rs` excluded as entry point not hazard; register now per §5; §4 docs trigger fires at this release's close.
risk_tier.b: Identical: warranted, family `destructive`, same surface and same exclusion of `src/cli/commands.rs`, register now rather than defer to the feature map, §4 docs trigger at this release's close (B also names the gate `segment-deletion` and gives the `risk_gate_add` call).

mandatory_controls.a: Three gate controls as required work — paper/sandbox env, human confirm naming the concrete effect, audit trail — with progressive exposure explicitly ruled off the floor as a "scale-to-harm judgment" and kill switch off-menu for destructive; plus the posture-conditional `[community-edition]` standing `auto:` line that `open-core` makes a MUST.
mandatory_controls.b: Four gate controls as required work — the same three plus progressive exposure, held warranted above the rule-of-thumb floor because a retention policy's blast radius is every series at once — kill switch likewise excluded; plus the same `[community-edition]` MUST.

divergences.governing_quote: **Rule of thumb:** money or destructive → at least paper env + human confirm + audit trail.
divergences.explanation: The same section carries two mechanisms that do not resolve each other: the menu's "Applies when" column lists Progressive exposure for "Money, destructive, ordering" — which reads as attaching it to this family — while the rule of thumb sets a three-control floor with "at least", and the surrounding text ("the deeper the harm, the more of them apply", "Do not apply all five to everything") delegates the remainder to an undecidable scale-to-harm judgment. Both planners read the floor identically and both correctly excluded the kill switch; they differ only on the delegated judgment, so neither misread a rule. §3's own worked `user-data-deletion` example registers "human confirm,audit trail,soft-delete window" — omitting paper env, below the stated floor, and adding a control absent from the menu — which further undercuts any binding reading. The divergence is consequential rather than cosmetic: bone-touch-judge.md §4.2 makes the registered control CSV "required work in the spine's plan, not advice", so the two planners commit the spine to different mandatory work.

secondary.topic: Whether rung 3 is still evaluated once rung 2 has already hit
secondary.a: "Rungs 3 and 4 are not reached" — the rung-2 bone-touch hit ends the ladder, so no separate bone-by-creation finding and no ADR obligation beyond the generic bone ceremony.
secondary.b: "Rung 3 is not idle here, even though rung 2 already decided the class" — rung 3 fires independently on the new unregistered `src/retention/policy.rs`, so the spine owes an ADR authored `Proposed` with its own declared touch surface.
secondary.governing_quote: Order matters: an earlier rung's verdict is not revisited by a later one.
secondary.explanation: Rung 1 carries an explicit halt ("Stop the ladder and go to §4"); rung 2 carries none — only "A hit → `bone`, regardless of the declared class, regardless of the critic" — and the quoted header sentence forbids a later rung *revisiting* the verdict without saying whether a later rung's separate obligations still attach. Rung 4's "If rungs 1-3 found nothing" and the §7 anti-pattern "A new bone with no touch surface. Then the next spine's rung 2 cannot see it" both support B's reading; nothing forecloses A's. The class verdict is unaffected (both `bone`, both with an ADR, since bone ceremony requires one either way), but only B's reading forces the ADR to declare a surface for the newly created bone — and here A's separately registered risk gate covers the same paths, so the practical gap largely closes by accident rather than by rule.

secondary.topic: Whether the §7c critic-veto pass is still owed after a bone-touch hit
secondary.a: Not mentioned; A states rungs 3 and 4 are not reached, and rung 4 is where class-declaration introduces the critic veto — A never affirmatively says the pass is skipped, so this is silence rather than a stated contrary position.
secondary.b: "Still owed, and independent: the §7c critic veto. A clean critic does not clear a touch hit."
secondary.governing_quote: Then the critic veto (`references/critic-veto.md`) may push `flesh → bone`. It never pushes `bone → flesh`; only an explicit, recorded user override does that.
secondary.explanation: The critic pass is a per-release step (SKILL.md §7c, critic-veto.md §1 "Fires: Once per release-planning pass"), but class-declaration introduces it only inside rung 4, so a reader who short-circuits the ladder at rung 2 can plausibly read the critic step as unreached — the same placement ambiguity as the rung-3 item above. Non-class findings still have to be routed (critic-veto §3), so treating the pass as unreached would drop release-level feedback, which is why this is worth recording even though it changes none of the five judgments.

notes: Four of five axes agree outright, including the two the scenario was built to stress (bone-touch overruling a declared `flesh`, and a destructive gate registered at first reach with an identical touch surface). The single divergence — whether progressive exposure is mandatory for a destructive gate — and both secondary items are prose ambiguities, not misreads: risk-gates §2 offers a per-control applicability column and a per-family "at least" floor without saying which binds, and class-declaration §1 never states whether the ladder halts on a rung-2 hit.
